note: All three findings in fix7/c4.json are re-issues of items wave 6 already closed (recorded in reports/coverage/fixes/w6-b0.json). Each was independently re-verified here rather than taken on trust: I read the current source, ran the guarding test, then severed the PRODUCTION wiring, watched the test fail, restored it, and watched it pass. All three hold. I then went looking for what wave 6 did NOT check on each: every other consumer of the changed value, and whether the fix inverted anything. That found one genuine unclosed residual inside finding 3's territory (AAVSO's own per-network notice names only the blocker Settings can fix and hides the one it cannot), which is fixed here with tests at both the service and the rendered-widget level.

fixes.title: Observing Alerts reports a First Light detection's brightness CHANGE as its apparent magnitude, so a self-discovered transient is announced as 'mag 2.4 NAKED EYE'
fixes.summary: Closed before this wave. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper.dart:48 sets `magnitude: null` (the pre-fix line was `final magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs();` at :20, passed to `magnitude:`), so the NAKED EYE / BINOCULAR / SMALL SCOPE bucketing in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/transients/widgets/transient_card.dart:580-588 can never run on a delta. The change itself is carried as its own labelled quantity: transient_alert_mapper.dart:32-36 builds 'D2.35 mag brighter than template', :54-56 appends it to the classification, and :57-63 spells out in the notes that it is a brightness change and not an apparent magnitude. I re-checked the three things wave 6 did not: (a) NO OTHER CALL SITE turns a delta into an apparent magnitude — transientAlertFromDetection is the only producer of a First Light TransientAlert (transient_alert_provider.dart:425), and the other deltaMag consumers all render it as a signed delta (transient_candidate_card.dart:183-200 '-0.50 mag', first_light_detail_screen.dart:227, cutout_strip.dart:55-58) while transient_report_service.dart:95-101 keeps the AAVSO magnitude on a real photometric zeropoint; (b) NO INVERSION — transient_alert_service.dart:733-736 and :780-786 both guard `alert.magnitude != null` before applying magnitudeThreshold, so a null magnitude keeps the alert in the feed and still notifies via :797, it only stops the bogus auto-queue at :790; (c) `peakMagnitude` is never set either, and the test asserts it.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper_test.dart (6 tests, incl. 'never reports a delta magnitude as an apparent magnitude' and 'a delta this large would be announced as naked-eye if kept', which asserts the exact bucket consequence rather than just non-nullness)
fixes.revert_check: Reverted transient_alert_mapper.dart:48 from `magnitude: null,` to `magnitude: detection.deltaMag?.abs(),`. 3 of 6 tests failed ('never reports a delta magnitude as an apparent magnitude', 'a delta this large would be announced as naked-eye if kept', 'a catalog-matched brightening keeps its name and gains the delta'). Restored byte-identically (md5 verified): all 6 pass.
fixes.caveats: Verified by source reading + revert check; not re-driven live.

fixes.title: The cull rail advertises 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' from a curve it already knows is stale; pressing it always refuses, and its advice ('re-integrate to refresh') reproduces the same stale curve
fixes.summary: Closed before this wave, and closed the right way round — the staleness test was MOVED to render time, not duplicated there. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:1536-1581 exposes `cullRecommendationOffer`, which applies every guard at build time (population length vs accepted length, duplicate accepted paths, any population path no longer accepted, keepN >= population.length, predictedSnrGainPct <= 0) and returns a CullOfferStatus of none/stale/alreadyOptimal/offerable. cullToRecommended() at :1589-1599 now switches on that same getter as its first statement instead of re-deriving the guards, so render and press cannot disagree. sub_cull_rail.dart:289 gates the pressable action on `_offer.isOfferable`; :503-513 renders a 'Cull analysis out of date' chip for stale and :515-533 a 'Keep-set already optimal' chip for the no-gain case, each with a tooltip that states the real numbers, instead of a quantified button. sub_cull_rail.dart:113-138 keeps `_offer` live by listening to the controller directly, so accepting/rejecting a sub retracts the action without a new curve having to arrive. Beyond wave 6 I confirmed there is NO SECOND CALL SITE: cullToRecommended has exactly one production caller (sub_cull_rail.dart:222), and the only other keepN surface, improvement_curve_panel.dart, is a descriptive chart that returns a placeholder for a curve with fewer than 2 points (:33) and offers no action at all.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/sub_cull_rail_stale_curve_test.dart (5 tests over a real SessionReviewController and a real in-memory database, with the real widget pumped against it — nothing stubbed)
fixes.revert_check: Reverted the production gate at sub_cull_rail.dart:289 from `_offer.isOfferable ? () => _cullToRecommended(_offer) : null` to `_offer.status != CullOfferStatus.none ? () => _cullToRecommended(_offer) : null` (the pre-fix condition: an action whenever a curve carries a keep-set). 4 of 5 tests failed, including 'a stale curve renders an out-of-date chip, not a quantified "Keep best N" action' and 'rejecting a sub stales the curve and retracts the action without a new curve arriving'. Restored byte-identically (md5 verified): all 5 pass.
fixes.caveats: Verified by source reading + revert check; not re-driven live (needs a session with real FITS subs).

fixes.title: In the Submit-discovery dialog all three network chips are dead on a default install, and only the currently-selected network's blocker is explained
fixes.summary: Closed before this wave. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/transient_report_panel.dart:131-139 passes `enabled: enabled` to SkotiqChip so an unavailable network renders as unavailable, and packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/components/skotiq_chip.dart:19-29,42-46,53-66,86-100 gives that flag real teeth — dimmed foreground and fill, halved border, `SystemMouseCursors.forbidden`, and a Semantics node announced as an enabled:false button (before, a null onTap alone produced a chip pixel-identical to an unselected-but-available one with no Semantics at all). transient_report_panel.dart:148-169 renders `_disabledNotices(...)` (:381-398) — one line per blocked format, collapsed to a single line when one blocker (unreviewed detection, or a dipole artefact) covers all three — instead of only the selected format's reason. The Preview/Copy/primary actions at :312-341 are SkotiqButtons whose null onPressed does render a disabled affordance (skotiq_button.dart:157,182,190,196,204,240). Beyond wave 6 I checked the OTHER CALL SITES of the same class: TransientSubmitDialog is a thin wrapper around this one panel (transient_submit_dialog.dart:44-47), and a scan of every SkotiqChip construction in packages/ and apps/desktop found no other site expressing 'disabled' via a conditional/null onTap, so this was the only consumer of the defect.
fixes.revert_check: Two independent severs, each restored byte-identically (md5 verified). (1) Removed `enabled: enabled,` from the chip construction at transient_report_panel.dart:135 -> 'a disabled AAVSO and MPC chip each state their own reason' failed on the enabled-flag assertion. (2) Replaced the `_disabledNotices(selected, scienceSettings)` call at :149 with the pre-fix single-reason expression `_formatEnabled(_format, ...) ? <String>[] : [_disabledReason(_format, ...)]` -> the same test failed on the missing AAVSO/MPC reasons. Both restored: all pass.
fixes.caveats: The filed defect is closed. One residual inside it was still open and is fixed in the next entry.

fixes.title: RESIDUAL of the above: AAVSO's per-network notice names only the blocker Settings can fix and hides the one it cannot, so the app sends the operator on a dead-end trip to Settings
fixes.summary: AAVSO requires BOTH a photometric zeropoint for the detection's frame and an observer code (transient_report_service.dart:95-101 + transient_report_panel.dart:374-376). On a fresh profile with an uncalibrated frame both are missing, but `aavsoDisabledReason` tested the observer code FIRST and returned early, so the panel rendered only 'AAVSO: Set your AAVSO observer code in Settings > Science first.' The operator goes and sets the one field the app pointed at, comes back, and AAVSO is still disabled behind an entirely different blocker no settings field can clear. This is the campaign's cry-wolf shape and it fooled the auditor too — finding 3's own text calls AAVSO 'the cheapest one to enable, it needs a single settings field', which is exactly what the app falsely told them. Fixed in the shared service so BOTH consumers get it: aavsoDisabledReason now collects every blocker that applies and states the un-fixable one first, because Settings cannot resolve it ('AAVSO needs a calibrated magnitude (a photometric zeropoint for this frame) - not available for this detection. Your AAVSO observer code is also unset (Settings > Science).'). The word 'first' is dropped when it is not the only blocker. When the observer code really is the only gap the original single sentence is returned unchanged. The two production consumers are packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/transient_report_panel.dart:426 (the rendered notice) and apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/first_light_handlers.dart:119 (the POST /api/firstlight/<id>/export/aavso 400 body) — both are fixed by the single service change; MPC's reason function was checked and already leads with its un-fixable blocker, so it needed nothing.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/transient_report_reasons_test.dart :: "AAVSO's notice names the blocker no setting can clear" — pumps the real TransientReportPanel over a fresh-profile ScienceSettings with no calibration rows and asserts the RENDERED text contains both 'photometric zeropoint' and 'observer code'. Plus packages/skotiq_core/test/services/transients/transient_report_service_test.dart :: 'disabled reason names BOTH blockers on a fresh, uncalibrated frame' (also asserts the string no longer says 'first'), 'disabled reason is the observer code alone when that is the only gap', and 'disabled reason is null once both requirements are met'.
fixes.revert_check: Wrote the widget test first and watched it fail against the unfixed tree (only the observer-code sentence was on screen). After the fix, reverted the body of aavsoDisabledReason to the original early-return form: the widget test 'AAVSO's notice names the blocker no setting can clear' failed AND the service test 'disabled reason names BOTH blockers on a fresh, uncalibrated frame' failed. Restored: all pass. The sever was on the production function both surfaces call, not on test-local logic.
fixes.caveats: packages/skotiq_core's full suite was run for the shared-file change: 6 pre-existing failures in test/services/import/nina_sequence_fidelity_test.dart ('SequenceImportValidationFailedException: Wait Has No Time Set', from sequence_importer.dart which is unmodified and last touched 2026-06-18) and a flaky-under-parallelism set in test/services/imaging_service_test.dart that passes when run alone (open task #12). Neither touches transients. dart analyze and dart format are clean on every changed file.
